answer: Each identity registers one velvet dye batch at the wharf, locks a 60-credit bond and pays a waste fee. The wharf weighs the waste, stamps a pearl seal on the manifest, and logs both weights. An auditor replays the log; a reused manifest or weight mismatch burns the bond. The k-th batch pays 25+4(k-1) credits, so the 1000th pays 4021 and 1000 fakes pay 2023000 in fees plus 60000 locked. A rented-manifest ring fails: the pearl seal binds one batch key to one waste weight, so a rented seal burns both bonds. An honest maker pays 25 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
